chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who entered into Islam and drank wine while he was ignorant (of the prohibition), he (peace be upon him) said: 'I would not establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him when he was ignorant, but I would inform him of that and teach him. So if he were to repeat, I would establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hadd for a new Muslim who drinks wine out of ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between ignorance of the ruling (jahal bi al-hukm) and ignorance of the prohibition itself, particularly for new converts. The Imam clarifies that the fixed penalty (Hadd) is suspended until the individual is explicitly informed, emphasizing education over immediate punishment. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on gradual spiritual integration and the removal of barriers to entry for new Muslims.
